items.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence is increasingly being integrated into instruction-driven task planning within various external environments, such as games, compilers, and Application Programming Interfaces. Obtaining planning scenarios from Large Language Model(LLM) greatly mitigates the time and computational costs associated with rule-based and network-based approaches, but still suffers from limited contextual horizons and a lack of real-time cognitive and interactive capabilities with real environments. The engineering application point of this paper is: To address the challenges, we introduce a large language model-based task planning agent to facilitate human-computer interaction and application of LLMs in real-world task planning activities, which has a generative memory (GM-Agent) that responds to the textualized reality of planning events. The contribution in GM-Agent leverages the inherent rules and worldviews extracted from textual data, employing generative memory modules to assimilate planning knowledge from expert experiences. This framework has demonstrated state-of-the-art performance in four out of five tasks set by LandWar, matching the performance of the Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback(RLHF) model in knowledge quiz tasks, despite having an equivalent number of parameters. Additionally, we have performed comprehensive comparison and ablation studies involving LLMs and various configurations, providing a detailed analysis of performance influencers and highlighting areas requiring further exploration.</jats:p>
title: Large Language Model-Based Planning Agent with Generative Memory Strengthens Performance in Textualized World
